title: Temurah 19
description: Abaye, Rava, Rav Ukva bar Ḥama and Ravina on when Rabbi Elazar lets the offspring of a female set aside for a male offering be sacrificed itself, then the mishna of a female set aside for a guilt offering, Rav’s “since the sanctity of value descends, inherent sanctity descends,” and why Rabbi Shimon disagrees.
topics: 🐑 A female set aside for a Paschal offering: before Passover and after it
🔁 Rava: a leftover Paschal offering is a peace offering; Abaye: the offspring goes where the leftover goes
🤰 Ravina: “it and its offspring” means it was pregnant, and a fetus is not its mother’s thigh
⚖️ Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina: Rabbi Elazar concedes about a female set aside for a guilt offering
📜 Mishna: a female for a guilt offering grazes until blemished; Rabbi Shimon: it is sold without a blemish
🪙 Rav: since the sanctity of value descends, inherent sanctity descends; Rava retracts to Rav Kahana
⏳ Rabbi Shimon: what is not fit in itself is not consecrated, and the animal whose time has not yet come learned from the firstborn

a1.he: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרַת וְלַד אָשָׁם, דְּלֵיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ, מוֹדֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דִּבְדָמָיו אִין הוּא עַצְמוֹ לָא קָרֵב.

a2.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְכִי בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ? וְהָא תַּנְיָא: הַמַּפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְפִסְחוֹ — תִּרְעֶה עַד (שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב) [שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב], וְתִמָּכֵר, וְיָבִיא בְּדָמֶיהָ פֶּסַח. יָלְדָה — יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיָבִיא בְּדָמָיו פֶּסַח.

a3.he: נִשְׁתַּיְּירָה אַחַר הַפֶּסַח, תִּרְעֶה עַד (שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב) [שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב], וְיָבִיא בְּדָמֶיהָ שְׁלָמִים. יָלְדָה, יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְיִמָּכֵר וְיָבִיא בְּדָמָיו שְׁלָמִים. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הוּא עַצְמוֹ יִקְרַב שְׁלָמִים.

a4.he: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּלֵיכָּא שֵׁם שְׁלָמִים עַל אִמּוֹ, וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר יִקְרַב שְׁלָמִים. אֲמַר לֵיהּ (רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר) [רָבָא]: ״אַחַר הַפֶּסַח״ קָא אָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי אַחַר הַפֶּסַח, דְּמוֹתַר פֶּסַח גּוּפֵיהּ קָרֵב שְׁלָמִים.

a5.he: אִי הָכִי, נִיפְלוֹג נָמֵי בְּרֵישָׁא! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, וּפְלִיגִי.

a6.he: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לָא פְּלִיג מִידֵּי, דִּגְמִירִי לִמְקוֹם שֶׁהַמּוֹתָר הוֹלֵךְ — הַוָּלָד הוֹלֵךְ; לְאַחַר הַפֶּסַח, דְּמוֹתָר קָרֵב שְׁלָמִים — וָלָד נָמֵי קָרֵב שְׁלָמִים.

a7.he: אֲבָל לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח, אִימֵּיהּ לְמַאי אַקְדְּשַׁהּ? לִדְמֵי פֶסַח, וָלָד נָמֵי לִדְמֵי פֶסַח.

a8.he: מֵתִיב רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן מִדְּאִימֵּיהּ לִדְמֵי, וָלָד נָמֵי לִדְמֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא: הַמַּפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לַפֶּסַח — הִיא וּוַלְדוֹתֶיהָ יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ, וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶם פֶּסַח. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הוּא עַצְמוֹ יִקְרַב פֶּסַח.

a9.he: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּאִימֵּיהּ לִדְמֵי, וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הוּא עַצְמוֹ קָרֵב פֶּסַח, וְלָא מוֹקְמִינַן לֵיהּ בְּאִימֵּיהּ!

a10.he: אָמַר רָבִינָא: בְּמַפְרִישׁ בְּהֵמָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת עָסְקִינַן, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר: אִם שִׁיְּירוֹ מְשׁוּיָּיר, דְּעוּבָּר לָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא, וְאִמּוֹ הִיא דְּלָא קָדְשָׁה קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף, אֲבָל הִיא קָדְשָׁה.

a11.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּבִבְהֵמָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת עָסְקִינַן, מִדְּקָתָנֵי ״הִיא וּוַלְדוֹתֶיהָ״, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

b1.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּמַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם דְּאֵין בְּנָהּ קָרֵב אָשָׁם. פְּשִׁיטָא! עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֶלָּא בְּמַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָה, דְּאִיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ, אֲבָל גַּבֵּי מַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם דְּלֵיכָּא שֵׁם אָשָׁם עַל אִמּוֹ — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מוֹדֶה דְּלֹא קָרֵב אָשָׁם!

b2.he: אִי לָאו דְּאַשְׁמְעִינַן, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּשֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲזֵי וָלָד לְהַקְרָבָה, וְהַאי נָמֵי הָא חֲזֵי לְהַקְרָבָה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b3.he: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּמַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאֵין בְּנָהּ קָרֵב אָשָׁם, נַישְׁמְעִינַן דְּאֵין בְּנָהּ קָרֵב עוֹלָה, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְאָשָׁם!

b4.he: אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן עוֹלָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: עוֹלָה הוּא דְּלָא קָרְבָה, דְּלָא אַקְדְּשַׁהּ לְאִמַּהּ (קְדוּשָּׁה עוּבָּרָהּ) [קְדוּשַּׁת עוֹלָה], אֲבָל אָשָׁם — [כֵּיוָן דְּאַקְדְּשַׁהּ לְאִימֵּיהּ לְאָשָׁם] — אֵימָא: וָלָד קָרֵב אָשָׁם, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b5.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם, תִּרְעֶה עַד שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב, וְתִימָּכֵר, וְיָבִיא בְּדָמֶיהָ אָשָׁם. וְאִם קָרַב אֲשָׁמוֹ, יִפְּלוּ דָּמָיו לִנְדָבָה.

b6.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תִּימָּכֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּמוּם.

b7.he: גְּמָ׳ וּלְמָה לִי תִּסְתָּאֵב? תִּימָּכֵר! כֵּיוָן דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְמִילְּתָא — הַיְינוּ מוּמָא!

b8.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: הַיְינוּ טַעַם דְּאָמְרִינַן, מִיגּוֹ דְּנָחֲתָא לַהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים — נָחֲתָא נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף. אָמַר רָבָא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת, הִקְדִּישׁ זָכָר לְדָמָיו — קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

b9.he: אִיתְּמַר: הִקְדִּישׁ זָכָר לְדָמָיו, רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף, רָבָא אָמַר: אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף. וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רָבָא לִדְרַב כָּהֲנָא, מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב.

b10.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תִּימָּכֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּמוּם. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִיגּוֹ דְּנָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים, תֵּיחוֹת לֵיהּ נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף!

b11.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: כֹּל מִידֵּי דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ לְגוּפֵיהּ — לָא נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף, דְּתַנְיָא: אָשָׁם בֶּן שָׁנָה וֶהֱבִיאוֹ בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם, בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם וֶהֱבִיאוֹ בֶּן שָׁנָה — כְּשֵׁירָה, וְלֹא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה.

b12.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עַצְמָן אֵינָן קְדוֹשִׁין.

b13.he: וַהֲרֵי מְחוּסַּר זְמַן, דְּלָא חֲזֵי, וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּקָדוֹשׁ, שָׁאנֵי מְחוּסַּר זְמַן, דַּחֲזֵי לִמְחַר.

b14.he: אִי הָכִי, אָשָׁם בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם וֶהֱבִיאוֹ בֶּן שָׁנָה, הָא חֲזֵי לְשָׁנָה, אֶלָּא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּמְחוּסַּר זְמַן, דְּיָלֵיף לֵיהּ מִבְּכוֹר.

b15.he: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מְחוּסַּר זְמַן נִכְנָס לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר, וַהֲרֵי הוּא כִּבְכוֹר, מָה בְּכוֹר קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ וְקָרֵב לְאַחַר זְמַנּוֹ, אַף מְחוּסַּר זְמַן קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ וְקָרֵב לְאַחַר זְמַנּוֹ.

messages.text: Continued from 18b: the Gemara contrasted Rabbi Elazar’s ruling that the offspring of a female set aside for a burnt offering is itself sacrificed with a later mishna (20b), where he says only that a burnt offering is brought with the money of the offspring of a guilt offering’s substitute. Rava has begun to answer: Rabbi Elazar says the offspring itself is offered as a burnt offering only where one set aside a female as a burnt offering, since there is burnt offering status for its mother.

But with regard to the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering, where there is no burnt offering status for its mother, as the animal for which it was substituted was a guilt offering, Rabbi Elazar concedes that an animal purchased with its money, received from selling the offspring, yes, it is sacrificed as a burnt offering, but the offspring itself is not sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.dh: אבל ולד תמורת אשם אין שם עולה על אמו
notes.he: הקדש ראשון שכולן באו מכחו לאשם הופרש ולאשם הקריבו ולא היה עולה הוא ולא דמיו. לשון ירושלמי ולריש שמעתין מהדר וכליל לאשים דברי הכל בתמיה כלומר אמאי לא פליגי רבנן בולדי תמורה כמו בולדי עולה:
notes.en: But with regard to the offspring of a guilt offering’s substitute, there is no burnt offering status for its mother: the first consecration, by whose force they all came, was designated as a guilt offering and was sacrificed as a guilt offering; it was not a burnt offering, neither it nor its value. In the Jerusalem version, the beginning of our passage [on 18b] goes back and asks, “And it is wholly burnt on the fires: is that the statement of all?” as a question, that is: why do the Rabbis not disagree about the offspring of substitutes as they do about the offspring of a burnt offering?

notes.he: אבל לרבנן ימכר וה"ה נמי לולד תמורת עולה ורישא רבי אליעזר היא:
notes.en: And it is Rabbi Elazar [Rashi: “R. A.”; on Rabba bar bar Ḥana’s answer, 18b]: but according to the Rabbis it is sold; and the same applies to the offspring of a burnt offering’s substitute, and the first clause is Rabbi Elazar’s.

notes.he: שניה היא להך קדמייתא דאפריש וקדמייתא דאפריש זכר הוה וקרב הילכך קרב נמי ולד תמורתו כו':
notes.en: The substitute of a burnt offering [on Rava’s answer, 18b]: it is second to that first animal that he designated, and the first one he designated was a male and was sacrificed. Therefore the offspring of its substitute is sacrificed too, etc.

notes.he: בעולת העוף ועוד דמיה לעולה קיימי הילכך נחתא לה קדושה לגופה הואיל ודוגמתה מצינו בעוף דקריבה משום הכי קרב ולד אבל ולד תמורת אשם ליכא שם עולה על הראשון שהיא אם לכולן שמכחו בא והוא קרב אשם ולא מצינו תמורת אשם קריבה בעולה הילכך לא נחתא קדושה על התמורה אלא לדמי ומשום הכי לא יקרב הולד:
notes.en: There is burnt offering status for its mother: in the bird burnt offering; moreover, its value stands to be a burnt offering. Therefore sanctity descends on its body, since we find its counterpart in a bird, which is sacrificed, and that is why the offspring is sacrificed. But with the offspring of a guilt offering’s substitute, there is no burnt offering status on the first animal, the mother of them all, by whose force it comes, and it was sacrificed as a guilt offering; and we do not find a guilt offering’s substitute sacrificed as a burnt offering. Therefore sanctity descends on the substitute only for its value, and that is why the offspring is not sacrificed.

messages.text: And does Rabbi Elazar require that there be burnt offering status for its mother, in order for the offspring to be sacrificed as a burnt offering? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: where there is no burnt offering status for its mother

messages.text: In the case of one who designates a female animal for his Paschal offering, which must be a male, the animal is left to graze until it becomes unfit, and it is then sold and he brings a Paschal offering with the money received for its sale.

notes.he: זכר:
notes.en: And he brings a Paschal offering with its money: a male.

messages.text: If the female animal gave birth to a male, the offspring may not be sacrificed as a Paschal offering despite the fact that it is a male. Rather, it is left to graze until it becomes unfit, and then it is sold and he brings a Paschal offering with the money received from its sale.

notes.he: ילדה קודם הפסח ירעה הולד עד שיסתאב כו':
notes.en: If it gave birth before Passover, the offspring grazes until it becomes unfit, etc.

messages.text: If the animal remained without a blemish until after Passover, it is left to graze until it becomes unfit, and he brings a peace offering with the money received for its sale. If it gave birth to a male after Passover, the offspring too is left to graze until it becomes unfit, and then it is sold, and he brings a peace offering with the money received for its sale.

notes.he: דפסח בשאר ימות השנה שלמים הוי כדאמרינן במנחות בשילהי פרק התודה (מנחות דף פג:) והיא גופה לא קרבה שלמים ואע"ג דשלמים באין נקבה הני הואיל ומחמת קדושה פסולה הויין ולא חזו לפסח אידחו נמי משלמים:
notes.en: If it remained after Passover, etc.: for a Paschal offering during the rest of the year is a peace offering, as we say in Menaḥot at the end of chapter HaToda (Menaḥot 83b). But it itself is not sacrificed as a peace offering. Although peace offerings come from females, these, since they became disqualified because of their sanctity and are not fit for a Paschal offering, are pushed away from being peace offerings too.

notes.he: אחר הפסח:
notes.en: It gave birth: after Passover.

notes.he: נשתיירה לאחר הפסח כגון שהביא פסח זכר אחר ונשתיירה זו נקבה לאחר הפסח תרעה עד שתסתאב ותמכר ויביא בדמיה שלמים דמותר פסח קרב שלמים. אבל היא עצמה שהפריש לפסח לא תקרב שלמים משום (דקדושה דחויה היא) [דפסח חובתו הוא] וכי הפריש נקבה לפסח לדמיה הפרישה ילדה לאחר הפסח ירעה כו':
notes.en: If it remained after Passover: for example, he brought another, male Paschal offering, and this female remained after Passover. It grazes until it becomes unfit, is sold, and he brings a peace offering with its money, since a leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed as a peace offering. But the animal itself that he designated for a Paschal offering is not sacrificed as a peace offering, [because the Paschal offering is his obligation]. And when he designated a female for a Paschal offering, he designated it for its value. If it gave birth after Passover, it grazes, etc.

messages.text: The offspring itself is sacrificed as a peace offering.
messages.lead: Rabbi Elazar disagrees in the latter case and says:

notes.he: ואע"ג דליכא שם שלמים על אמו דהא לשם פסח אקדשה:
notes.en: It itself is sacrificed as a peace offering: even though there is no peace offering status for its mother, since it was consecrated as a Paschal offering.

messages.text: But here, it is a case where there is no peace offering status for its mother, as the mother was consecrated as a Paschal offering, and yet Rabbi Elazar says that the offspring is sacrificed as a peace offering.
messages.quote: itself is sacrificed as a peace offering

notes.dh: והא הכא דליכא שם שלמים על אמו
notes.he: כאן נוכל להעמיד שפיר השתי לשונות שהרי אין שלמים בעופות וגבי תחילת הקדש לא לשם שלמים הופרש:
notes.en: But here, where there is no peace offering status for its mother: here we can properly sustain both versions [of Rashi’s explanation of “burnt offering status for its mother,” on 18b], since there are no peace offerings from birds, and at the start of the consecration it was not designated for a peace offering.

notes.dh: והא הכא דליכא שם שלמים על אמו
notes.he: שלא הפרישה תחלה לאמו לשם שלמים אלא לשם פסח ועוד שלא הפרישה אלא לדמיה:
notes.en: But here, where there is no peace offering status for its mother: since he did not designate the mother at first for the sake of a peace offering but for the sake of a Paschal offering; moreover, he designated it only for its value.

messages.text: @Abaye Do you say that this statement of Rabbi Elazar with regard to a Paschal offering after Passover contradicts my explanation? Not so; the status of a Paschal offering after Passover is different, as a leftover Paschal offering itself is sacrificed as a peace offering. Therefore, a female animal designated as a Paschal offering has the status of a peace offering after Passover.

notes.he: כגון אם הפריש פסח ונתכפר באחר וניתותר זה קרב שלמים הילכך הך דניתותרה לאחר הפסח שם שלמים עלה ואזיל ליה שם פסח מינה וחייל עליה שם שלמים אלא שאינה יכולה ליקרב נקבה הואיל ומכח פסח אתא:
notes.en: After Passover is different, as a leftover Paschal offering: for example, if he designated a Paschal offering and achieved atonement with another, and this one was left over, it is sacrificed as a peace offering. Therefore this one, left over after Passover, has peace offering status on it: the name of Paschal offering departs from it and the name of peace offering takes effect on it, except that it cannot be sacrificed as a female, since it came by the force of a Paschal offering.

notes.he: א"ל שאני אחר הפסח אמאי יקרב שלמים דמותר פסח גופיה קרב שלמים ודמי [כמאן דאיכא שם שלמים על אמו אי הכי כיון דאמרת דמותר פסח יקרב שלמים גופיה] נפלוג נמי ברישא בולדה קודם הפסח דהא ולד הוי מותר פסח ולימא ר' אליעזר דיקרב הוא גופיה שלמים:
notes.en: He said to him: after Passover is different. Why is it sacrificed as a peace offering? Because a leftover Paschal offering itself is sacrificed as a peace offering, [and it is like a case where there is peace offering status for its mother. If so, since you say that a leftover Paschal offering itself is sacrificed as a peace offering,] let him also disagree in the first clause, where it gave birth before Passover, since the offspring is a leftover Paschal offering, and let Rabbi Elazar [Rabbeinu Gershom: “Rabbi Eliezer”] say that it itself is sacrificed as a peace offering.

notes.he: דכיון דילדה אחר הפסח דמי כמקדיש פסח בשאר ימות השנה דקרב שלמים אף האי נמי קרב עצמו שלמים (ואי) [והיינו] טעמא דר' אלעזר [גבי עולה] כיון דאיכא שם עולה על אמו שכן מצינו עולה נקבה בעוף הילכך קדשה לגופה ולד נמי קדיש וקרב:
notes.en: A Paschal offering is different: since it gave birth after Passover, it is like one who consecrates a Paschal offering during the rest of the year, which is sacrificed as a peace offering; so this one too is itself sacrificed as a peace offering. [And this is] the reason of Rabbi Elazar [regarding a burnt offering]: since there is burnt offering status for its mother, as we find a female burnt offering among birds, it is therefore consecrated in its body, and the offspring too is consecrated and sacrificed.

messages.text: If so, that the reason Rabbi Elazar permits the offspring to be sacrificed is that the mother also has the status of a peace offering, let Rabbi Elazar also disagree with the Rabbis in the first clause of the baraita, where the female animal designated as a Paschal offering gave birth before Passover. Rabbi Elazar should state that this offspring itself may be brought as a peace offering, as here too the mother has the status of a peace offering, since a Paschal offering slaughtered before Passover as a peace offering is valid.
messages.quote: a leftover Paschal offering itself is sacrificed as a peace offering

notes.he: דטעמיה דר"א משום דאיכא שם שלמים על אמו לפלוג נמי ברישא ילדה קודם הפסח ונימא רבי אליעזר הוא עצמו יקרב דהולד עצמו יקרב שלמים דקודם פסח נמי אי שחיט לפסח לשם שלמים כשר דפסח בשאר ימות השנה שלא בי"ד בניסן שלמים הוא והילכך שם שלמים על אמו:
notes.en: If so: if Rabbi Elazar’s [Rashi: “Rabbi Eliezer”] reason is that there is peace offering status for its mother, let him also disagree in the first clause, where it gave birth before Passover, and let Rabbi Elazar say that the offspring itself is sacrificed as a peace offering. For before Passover too, if one slaughtered the Paschal offering for the sake of a peace offering it is valid, since a Paschal offering during the rest of the year, not on the fourteenth of Nisan, is a peace offering. Hence there is peace offering status for its mother.

notes.he: פרש"י (לשון ראשון) ילדה לפני הפסח נימא רבי אליעזר הוא עצמו יקרב פסח דהא איכא שם פסח על אמו אלא שאינה יכולה ליקרב והכא אין יכולין להעמיד לשון ראשון דרש"י דלעיל דשם עולת העוף על אמו דהא הכא אין פסח בא נקבה דאין פסח בעופות אבל לשון שני ניחא שהרי תחילת הקדש לשם פסח הופרש והוה ליה לומר דהולד יקריב לשם פסח וא"ת לישני ליה דבעינן שם פסח על אמו בשום מקום ולא אשכחן ליה הכא דאין שם פסח על נקבה ליקרב היא עצמה ומשום הכי אין הולד קרב הוא עצמו לשם פסח מכאן אומר הרמ"ר דלעולם לא אמר דמהני שם עולת העוף על אמו להכשיר הוולד עצמו וכל היכא דאשכחנא להאי לישנא נפרשהו בע"ה וברישא פירש יפה:
notes.en: If so, let him also disagree in the first clause: Rashi explained (first version): if it gave birth before Passover, let Rabbi Elazar [Tosafot: “Rabbi Eliezer”] say that the offspring itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering, since there is Paschal status for its mother, except that it cannot be sacrificed. Here we cannot sustain Rashi’s first version above, that bird burnt offering status for its mother [counts], since here no Paschal offering comes from a female, as there is no Paschal offering from birds. But the second version works well, since at the start of the consecration it was designated for a Paschal offering, and he should have said that the offspring is sacrificed as a Paschal offering. And if you will say: let him answer that we need Paschal status for its mother somewhere, and we do not find it here, since there is no Paschal status by which a female itself is sacrificed, and that is why the offspring itself is not sacrificed as a Paschal offering — from here the RaMaR says that we never say that bird burnt offering status for its mother helps to make the offspring itself fit, and wherever we find this expression we will explain it, with God’s help. And in the first clause he explained well.

notes.he: ואם תאמר מאי אי הכי איכא הכא דהכי נמי מצי לפרוכי ממתני' בהדיא מ"ש במפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה אמר רבי אליעזר דבנה עצמו קרב עולה והכא גבי פסח אמר ירעה ויש לומר דה"פ אי אמרת בשלמא בלאו האי שינויא דרבא לא מצי למיפרך ממתניתין דשאני התם דאם הולד קרב עולה אין שם עולה נעקר מן האם דלעולם אדם יכול להקריב עולה בכל יום אבל הכא דאם הולד עצמו קרב פסח נמצא שם פסח נעקר מן האם ממנה ומדמיה שהרי אין בידו להקריב רק פסח אחד לפיכך אין להקריב הולד בפסח לעקור ממה שהופרשה אבל לרבא פריך שפיר מאחר דאית ליה דמשום דמותר פסח קרב שלמים חשיב ליה כאילו הוי שם שלמים על אמו ה"נ הוה ליה למימר מהאי טעם קודם פסח נמי שיהא הולד עצמו קרב פסח ולא כפרש"י שפירש ניפלוג נמי ברישא ונימא הולד עצמו יקרב שלמים קודם פסח דקודם פסח נמי אם שחט פסח לשם שלמים כשר דפסח בשאר ימות השנה (קרבה שלמים) שלא בארבעה עשר בניסן קרב שלמים הילכך שם שלמים על אמו:
notes.en: If so: And if you will say: what is the “if so” here? He could just as well have challenged directly from the mishna: why is it that with one who designates a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth, Rabbi Elazar said its offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering, while here, with a Paschal offering, he said it grazes? One can say this is the meaning: granted, without this answer of Rava he could not challenge from the mishna, since there it is different: if the offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering, burnt offering status is not uprooted from the mother, as a person can always sacrifice a burnt offering any day. But here, if the offspring itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering, Paschal status turns out to be uprooted from the mother, from it and from its value, since he can sacrifice only one Paschal offering; therefore the offspring is not sacrificed as a Paschal offering, uprooting [the mother] from what it was designated for. But according to Rava he challenges well: since he holds that because a leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed as a peace offering it is considered as though there were peace offering status for its mother, he should likewise have said, for this reason, that before Passover too the offspring itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering. And not as Rashi explained, who explained: let him disagree in the first clause too and say that the offspring itself is sacrificed as a peace offering before Passover, since before Passover too, if one slaughtered a Paschal offering for the sake of a peace offering it is valid, for a Paschal offering during the rest of the year, not on the fourteenth of Nisan, is sacrificed as a peace offering; therefore there is peace offering status for its mother.

notes.he: בילדה קודם הפסח דהוא עצמו יקרב שלמים דהא איכא [הכא] שם שלמים על אמו שהרי נקבה ישנה בשלמים:
notes.en: Let Rabbi Elazar also disagree in the first clause: where it gave birth before Passover, that it itself be sacrificed as a peace offering, since there is peace offering status for its mother [here], as females are found among peace offerings.

messages.text: Yes, it is indeed so, and they disagree in this case as well.

notes.he: דפליג ברישא:
notes.en: Indeed so: that he disagrees in the first clause.

notes.he: אלא אמתין כו':
notes.en: Indeed so, that he disagrees. [The printed edition’s editor suggests reading: but he waits to disagree until the latter clause.] But he waited, etc.

messages.text: In a case where the female animal designated as a Paschal offering gave birth before Passover, there is nobody who disagrees; rather, they all agree that the offspring may not be sacrificed. As it is learned as a tradition that to the place that the leftover offering goes, the offspring goes as well. Therefore, after Passover, when the leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed as a peace offering, the offspring is also sacrificed as a peace offering.
messages.lead: Abaye suggested another explanation of the opinion of Rabbi Elazar and said:

notes.he: דטעמיה דר' אליעזר לאו משום דאיכא שם שלמים על אמו אלא טעמיה דרבי אליעזר בכולהו משום דגמירי למקום שהמותר הולך אם היה מפריש ב' בהמות לאחריות אם אבדה והפריש ונתכפר באחרת ונמצאת ראשונה למקום שאותו מותר הולך הולד הולך הילכך גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה כי היכי דאם הפריש עולה ונתכפר באחרת קריבה השניה עולה דהא נדבה נינהו ותרוייהו חזו ולד דעולה נמי אם הפריש נקבה לעולה קרב דומיא דמותר גבי אשם נמי דמותר אשם רועה ולד תמורת אשם נמי רועה וגבי פסח נמי אחר הפסח דמותר הפסח דינו ליקרב לכתחילה שלמים אם נתכפר באחר ולד נמי קרב שלמים קודם הפסח דמותר לא חזי למידי כגון אם הפריש ב' פסחים לאחריות לא חזו לשלמים לכתחילה דסתמייהו לפסח וחד מינייהו דהוי מותר לא חזי לפסח דהא ב' פסחים לא יקריב הילכך ולד פסח נמי לא חזי למידי אלא אזיל בתר אימיה דקדושה לדמי פסח והא נמי קדיש לדמי פסח:
notes.en: Abaye said: nobody disagrees at all: Rabbi Elazar’s reason is not that there is peace offering status for its mother. Rather, his reason in all these cases is that it is learned as a tradition: to the place that the leftover goes [the offspring goes]. If he designated two animals as a guarantee, or if one was lost and he designated another and achieved atonement with the other, and then the first was found, then the offspring goes to the place that this leftover goes. Therefore, with one who designates a female for a burnt offering: just as, if he designated a burnt offering and achieved atonement with another, the second is sacrificed as a burnt offering, since they are gift offerings and both are fit, so the offspring of the burnt offering, where he designated a female for a burnt offering, is sacrificed too, like the leftover. With a guilt offering too: since a leftover guilt offering grazes, the offspring of a guilt offering’s substitute grazes as well. And with a Paschal offering, after Passover: since the law of a leftover Paschal offering is to be sacrificed as a peace offering from the outset if he achieved atonement with another, the offspring too is sacrificed as a peace offering. Before Passover, the leftover is fit for nothing: for example, if he designated two Paschal offerings as a guarantee, they are not fit as peace offerings from the outset, since unspecified they stand for the Paschal offering, and the one of them that is left over is not fit for a Paschal offering, as he may not sacrifice two Paschal offerings. Therefore the offspring of the Paschal offering too is fit for nothing; rather it follows its mother, which is consecrated for the value of a Paschal offering, and this one too is consecrated for the value of a Paschal offering.

notes.dh: אביי אומר לא פליג מידי למקום שהמותר הולך שם הולד הולך
notes.he: אביי לא לפרש כל דבריו של ר"א גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה וכן מפריש נקבה לפסח ונשתיירה בהני שני מקומות אמר דהולד עצמו קרב שהרי אם לא נעקרה מקדושתה במפריש נקבה לעולה דמיה לא ידחו מהיות עולה וכן מפריש נקבה לפסח ונשתיירה וילדה אם בנה קרב לא ידחה האם משלמים דכיון שעבר הפסח אינה ראויה כ"א לשלמים אבל גבי תמורת אשם וכן הפריש נקבה לפסחו וילדה קודם הפסח דבשניהם אמר ר"א דהולד ירעה היינו משום דאם הולד דתמורת אשם היה קרב א"כ ידחה אמה ממה שהופרשה תחילה דהיינו אשם שהרי אינו יכול להקריב שני אשמות וכן מפריש נקבה לפסחו וילדה קודם הפסח אם יקרב הולד הוא עצמו אם כן ידחה אמו היא ודמיה מפסח דאינו יכול להביא כי אם פסח אחד בשנה כך שמעתי מיהו אין לשון הש"ס ממש מיושב על זה וגם רש"י לא פירש כן:
notes.en: Abaye says: nobody disagrees at all; to the place that the leftover goes, the offspring goes: Abaye [comes] to explain all of Rabbi Elazar’s words. With one who designates a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth, and likewise one who designates a female for a Paschal offering and it remained, in these two places he said the offspring itself is sacrificed, since [the mother] is not uprooted from its sanctity: with one who designates a female for a burnt offering, its value will not be pushed away from being a burnt offering; and likewise with one who designates a female for a Paschal offering and it remained and gave birth, if its offspring is sacrificed the mother is not pushed away from being a peace offering, since once Passover has passed it is fit only for a peace offering. But with a guilt offering’s substitute, and likewise one who designated a female for his Paschal offering and it gave birth before Passover, where in both Rabbi Elazar said the offspring grazes, that is because if the offspring of the guilt offering’s substitute were sacrificed, its mother would be pushed away from what it was first designated for, namely a guilt offering, as one cannot sacrifice two guilt offerings; and likewise with one who designates a female for his Paschal offering and it gave birth before Passover, if the offspring itself were sacrificed, its mother, it and its value, would be pushed away from the Paschal offering, as one can bring only one Paschal offering a year. So I heard. However, the wording of the Talmud does not really fit this, and Rashi too did not explain it so.

notes.he: ברישא אלא בסיפא וטעמא מאי משום דגמירי למקום שהמותר הולך לשם הולד הולך:
notes.en: Abaye said: nobody disagrees at all: in the first clause, only in the latter clause. And what is the reason? Because it is learned as a tradition that to the place that the leftover goes, the offspring goes.

messages.text: But before Passover, when the Paschal offering is not yet considered leftover, the offspring is endowed with the same sanctity as the mother. In what way is the mother consecrated? It is consecrated for the value of a Paschal offering, that is, so that it should be sold and a Paschal offering should be purchased with the proceeds, as the female animal itself may not be sacrificed as a Paschal offering. If so, the offspring as well is consecrated only for the value of a Paschal offering.

notes.he: וכשנשתיירה שלא נתק לרעיה עד לאחר הפסח (לאחר הפסח) דמותר פסח קרב שלמים כדאמרינן [נשתיירה] (ולד שיירה) לאחר הפסח תרעה עד שתסתאב ותמכר ויביא בדמיה שלמים [וולד] נמי קרב שלמים הוא עצמו אבל ילדה לפני הפסח דאימיה למאי אקדשה אלא לדמי דכיון [דכל כמה דלא אקריב לפסח] (דפסח) חובתו היא דמידע ידע דנקבה לא הויא (פסח) [אלא לדמי] ש"מ כי אקדשה לדמי פסח אקדשה (ותימני) [ומדאימיה] דמי פסח ולד נמי לדמי פסח אקדשיה ודיניה כאמו ולא קרב עצמו שלמים הילכך לא פליג ברישא. ל"א והא פסח נקבה דליכא שם שלמים על אמו שלא הפרישה לשם שלמים אלא לשם פסח (ולא קדיש) [ולהקדש] גופה דנקבה [לא חזי] אלא לדמים כדאמרן ואפילו הכי ולדה קאמר רבי אלעזר דקדיש גופיה לשלמים אע"ג דליכא שם שלמים על אמו:
notes.en: And when it remained, not set aside to graze until after Passover, since a leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed as a peace offering, as we said: if it remained after Passover, it grazes until it becomes unfit, is sold, and he brings a peace offering with its money, [and the offspring] too is itself sacrificed as a peace offering. But if it gave birth before Passover — for what was its mother consecrated? Only for its value, since [as long as he has not sacrificed his Paschal offering] it is his obligation, and he knows full well that a female cannot be [a Paschal offering, only for its value]. Conclude that when he consecrated it, he consecrated it for the value of a Paschal offering; [and since its mother is] for the value of a Paschal offering, he consecrated the offspring too for the value of a Paschal offering, and its law is like its mother’s, and it is not itself sacrificed as a peace offering. Therefore he does not disagree in the first clause. Another version: but [here is] a female Paschal offering, where there is no peace offering status for its mother, since he did not designate it for the sake of a peace offering but for the sake of a Paschal offering, [and to consecrate] the body of a female [is not fitting], only for its value, as we said; and even so Rabbi Elazar says its offspring is itself consecrated as a peace offering, although there is no peace offering status for its mother.

notes.dh: אביי אמר היינו טעמא דלא פליג
notes.he: ברישא אלא בסיפא דקסבר למקום שמותר הולך לשם ולד הולך מותר אשם דלא קרב אשם לאחר שנתכפרו בעליו כדאמרינן במתני' אלא ירעה ולד דתמורת אשם נמי ירעה וכן מותר פסח לאחר הפסח [דהוא עצמו קרב שלמים ולד נמי יקרב שלמים] אבל ברישא ילדה לפני הפסח אימיה למאי אקדשה לדמי כו'. כדאמרן בלישנא קמא. רבי אלעזר אומר הוא עצמו הולד זכר יקרב פסח ולא מוקמינן ליה באימיה. כלומר דלא אמרינן מה אמו אינה מקודשת אלא לדמים אף בנה נמי:
notes.en: Abaye said: this is the reason he does not disagree in the first clause but in the latter clause: he holds that to the place that the leftover goes, the offspring goes. A leftover guilt offering is not sacrificed as a guilt offering after its owner has achieved atonement, as we say in the mishna, but grazes; the offspring of a guilt offering’s substitute grazes too. And likewise a leftover Paschal offering after Passover, [which itself is sacrificed as a peace offering; the offspring too is sacrificed as a peace offering]. But in the first clause, where it gave birth before Passover — for what was its mother consecrated? For its value, etc., as we said in the first version. Rabbi Elazar says: the male offspring itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering, and we do not establish it like its mother; that is, we do not say: just as its mother is consecrated only for its value, so too its offspring.

messages.text: And do we say that Rabbi Elazar maintains that as its mother is consecrated only for the value of a Paschal offering, the offspring as well is consecrated only for the value of a Paschal offering? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.lead: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama raises an objection to this explanation of Abaye:
messages.quote: the offspring as well is consecrated only for the value of a Paschal offering

messages.text: One who designates a female animal as a Paschal offering, it and its offspring are left to graze until they become unfit, and then they are sold, and he brings a Paschal offering with the money received for their sale.
The offspring itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering.

But here it is a case where its mother was consecrated for the value of a Paschal offering, and nevertheless Rabbi Elazar said that the offspring itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering, and we do not establish the status of the offspring based upon the sanctity of the mother.

notes.he: ל"א והא מותר פסח כו':
notes.en: Another version: “But a leftover Paschal offering,” etc.

messages.text: One can answer that here we are dealing with a case of one who designates a pregnant animal, and Rabbi Elazar holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said with regard to one who consecrates a pregnant animal for a specific purpose, that if he left it out, i.e., designated the fetus as having a different sanctity, it is left out from the sanctity of the mother and consecrated in accordance with the designated sanctity.

notes.he: המקדיש בהמה מעוברת ושייר עוברה לקדושה אחרת משוייר אלמא תרי גופי נינהו והילכך כי לא שייריה נמי לאו גופא דאם הוא ולאו מכחה דאם אתי ועליה דידיה חיילא קדושת פסח:
notes.en: If he left it out, it is left out: one who consecrates a pregnant animal and leaves its fetus out for a different sanctity, it is left out. Evidently they are two bodies. Therefore, even when he did not leave it out, it is not the mother’s body and does not come by the mother’s force, and the sanctity of a Paschal offering takes effect on it in its own right.

notes.he: אמאי קאמר ר' אלעזר הכא הוא עצמו יקרב פסח כגון דאפרשיה נקבה מעוברת לפסחו דאקדיש נמי עובר:
notes.en: Ravina said: with what are we dealing here? Why does Rabbi Elazar say here that it itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering? For example, where he set aside a pregnant female for his Paschal offering, so that he consecrated the fetus too.

messages.text: The reason is that a fetus is not considered the thigh of its mother, but rather the mother and its offspring are considered two separate animals. Here too, it is only its mother that is not sanctified with the inherent sanctity of a Paschal offering, but only for the value of a Paschal offering, as it is female. But the offspring is consecrated as a Paschal offering.

notes.dh: ור' אלעזר סבר לה כר' יוחנן
notes.he: דאמר אם שיירו משוייר [ועובר לאו ירך אמו הוא] כדאמר ר' יוחנן הפריש חטאת מעוברת וילדה רצה מתכפר בה רצה מתכפר בולדה ועובר לאו ירך אמו אלא דמי כמאן דאקדשיה לעובר לחודיה הילכך אע"ג דהוא לא קדש קדושת הגוף אלא לדמים מ"מ הולד קדוש וקרב פסח. אבל הפריש נקבה ואח"כ נתעברה ההוא ירך אמו הוא ולא קרב פסח:
notes.en: And Rabbi Elazar holds in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said: if he left it out, it is left out, [and a fetus is not its mother’s thigh], as Rabbi Yoḥanan said: if one set aside a pregnant animal as a sin offering and it gave birth, if he wishes he achieves atonement with it, and if he wishes he achieves atonement with its offspring; and a fetus is not its mother’s thigh but is like one who consecrated the fetus by itself. Therefore, although it [the mother] was consecrated not with inherent sanctity but only for its value, the offspring is nevertheless consecrated and is sacrificed as a Paschal offering. But if he set aside a female and it became pregnant afterward, that offspring is its mother’s thigh and is not sacrificed as a Paschal offering.

messages.text: @Ravina This, too, stands to reason, that we are dealing with a case where he designated a pregnant animal, from the fact that the baraita teaches: It and its offspring. This indicates that both the mother and its offspring were in existence at the time of the consecration.

notes.he: משמע ששניהן היו בשעת הקדש מדלא תני המפריש נקבה לפסחו תרעה ילדה זכר ירעה כדקתני לעיל:
notes.en: It and its offspring: implies that both existed at the time of the consecration, since it does not teach, “One who designates a female for his Paschal offering, it grazes; if it gave birth to a male, it grazes,” as it taught above.

messages.text: Conclude from here that this explanation is correct.

And Rabbi Elazar concedes to the opinion of the Rabbis with regard to a case where one designates a female animal for a guilt offering, which is only brought from a male animal, that its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering.

notes.dh: אמר רבי יוסי בר' חנינא ומודה רבי אליעזר
notes.he: אע"ג דגבי מפריש נקבה לעולה אמר דהולד עצמו יקרב עולה מפריש נקבה לאשם מודה הוא דאין בנה קרב אשם אף קודם כפרה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: And Rabbi Elazar concedes: although with one who designates a female for a burnt offering he said that the offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering, with one who designates a female for a guilt offering he concedes that its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, even before atonement.

messages.text: Isn’t that obvious? As Rabbi Elazar states that the offspring may be sacrificed only if one designates a female animal for a burnt offering and it gives birth, due to the fact that there is burnt offering status for a bird that is the same sex as its mother. But with regard to one who designates a female animal as a guilt offering, where there is no guilt offering status for its mother, even Rabbi Elazar concedes that its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering.
messages.quote: its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering

notes.he: בעולת העוף:
notes.en: That there is burnt offering status for its mother: in the bird burnt offering.

notes.he: דלא מצינו אשם נקבה הילכך לא חל עליה שם אשם:
notes.en: There is no guilt offering status for its mother: since we do not find a female guilt offering, guilt offering status therefore does not take effect on it.

notes.he: פשיטא עד כאן לא קאמר רבי אליעזר התם אלא גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה דאיכא שם עולה על אמו כו' - הכא לא מצינו לפרושי כלשון שני דרש"י דלעיל ולומר דתחילת הקדש האם לשם עולה הופרש שהרי מפריש נקבה לאשם נמי תחילת הקדש האם לשם אשם הופרש ולפי זה היה לנו לומר דבנה קרב באשם אלא דע"כ שאנו צריכין לפרש לשון ראשון של רש"י ולומר דאיכא שם עולה על אמו בעולת העוף ותימה דהיכי עביד פשיטא מיניה ועוד דלעיל פירשתי דעולת העוף על אמו לא מהני להכשיר הולד ונראה למורי לפרש דאיכא שם עולה על אמו דסוף האם להיות דמיה לעולה לפיכך דין הולד ליקרב עולה כאמו אבל גבי נקבה לאשם אם יקרב הולד אשם לא יהיה כאמו שהרי ידחה האם מאשם ותהא דמי עולה ואין זה דין לחלק חילוק הולד מדין אמו ואע"ג דלעיל אסיק רבא גבי מפריש נקבה לפסחו דפליג ר"א ארישא פי' אם ילדה קודם הפסח וקרב הולד עצמו פסח אע"ג דסוף האם להיות שלמים היינו משום דמותר הפסח קרב שלמים וחשיב להו רבא בחד:
notes.en: Obvious; Rabbi Elazar says his ruling there only with regard to one who designates a female for a burnt offering, where there is burnt offering status for its mother, etc.: Here we cannot explain in accordance with Rashi’s second version above and say that the mother’s initial consecration was designated for a burnt offering, since with one who designates a female for a guilt offering too, the mother’s initial consecration was designated for a guilt offering, and by that reasoning we would have to say that its offspring is sacrificed as a guilt offering. Rather, we are forced to explain in accordance with Rashi’s first version and say that there is burnt offering status for its mother in the bird burnt offering. But it is puzzling: how does he make it “obvious” from that? Moreover, above I explained that bird burnt offering status for its mother does not help to make the offspring fit. My teacher sees fit to explain: “there is burnt offering status for its mother” because in the end the mother’s value goes for a burnt offering; therefore the offspring’s law is to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, like its mother. But with a female set aside for a guilt offering, if the offspring were sacrificed as a guilt offering it would not be like its mother, since the mother would be pushed away from the guilt offering and become the value of a burnt offering, and it is not right to distinguish the offspring’s law from its mother’s. And although Rava concluded above, with one who designates a female for his Paschal offering, that Rabbi Elazar disagrees in the first clause too, meaning that if it gave birth before Passover the offspring itself is sacrificed as a Paschal offering even though in the end the mother is to be a peace offering, that is because a leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed as a peace offering, and Rava counts them as one.

notes.he: דליכא שם אשם על אמו דלא אשכחן אשם נקבה:
notes.en: Where there is no guilt offering status for its mother: since we do not find a female guilt offering.

notes.he: ל"א פשיטא ע"כ לא אמר ר' אלעזר דולד קרב אלא במפריש נקבה לעולה דאי למ"ד משום דאיכא שם עולה על אמו ואי משום דמותר עולה עולה אבל מפריש נקבה לאשם דליכא שם אשם על אמו ומותר אשם לא קרב אשם ולד [נמי] לא קדיש לקרב ולא איצטריך למימר ומודה ר' אלעזר:
notes.en: Another version: Obvious; Rabbi Elazar said that the offspring is sacrificed only with one who designates a female for a burnt offering, whether according to the one who says it is because there is burnt offering status for its mother, or because a leftover burnt offering is a burnt offering. But with one who designates a female for a guilt offering, where there is no guilt offering status for its mother and a leftover guilt offering is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, the offspring [too] is not consecrated to be sacrificed, and there was no need to say, “And Rabbi Elazar concedes.”

messages.text: This statement is nevertheless necessary, for if Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, had not informed us of this halakha, I would say that the reason for the ruling of Rabbi Elazar, that one who designates a female animal for a burnt offering may sacrifice the offspring as a burnt offering, is not due to the fact that there is burnt offering status for a bird with the same sex as its mother; rather it is because the offspring is fit as an offering, as it is a male, and this too, the offspring of the female that was designated as a guilt offering, is likewise fit as an offering, as it is a male. Therefore, he teaches us that this offspring is not sacrificed even according to the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.

notes.he: וליקרב אשם:
notes.en: And this too is fit as an offering: and let it be sacrificed as a guilt offering.

notes.he: דטעמיה דרבי אליעזר משום דאיכא שם עולה על אמו והא ליכא שם אשם על אמו:
notes.en: He teaches us: that Rabbi Elazar’s [Rashi: “Rabbi Eliezer”] reason is that there is burnt offering status for its mother, and here there is no guilt offering status for its mother.

notes.he: דזכר הוא והאי נמי ולד אשם דזכר הוא וחזי להקרבה ואימא ליקרב אשם להכי איצטריך למימר ומודה ר' אלעזר:
notes.en: [Rather, because] the offspring is fit as an offering: as it is a male. And this one too, the offspring of a guilt offering, is a male and fit as an offering, and I might say: let it be sacrificed as a guilt offering. That is why he needed to say, “And Rabbi Elazar concedes.”

notes.he: סד"א טעמא דר' אלעזר הוא דליקרב בנה אשם [משום] ובאשם נמי ליקרב דקסבר כיון דאקדשה לאימיה קדושת דמים דאשם היינו חובתו ואשם לא קרב נקבה ולא קדשה אלא לדמים ומגו דקדש קדושת דמים קדיש קדושת הגוף ונחתא ליה לולד דהא חזי דזכר הוא וליקרב להכי איצטריך ומודי ר' אלעזר:
notes.en: It was necessary: you might have thought that Rabbi Elazar’s reason is that its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering because, since the sanctity of value descends on it, inherent sanctity descends on it too; and with a guilt offering too, let it be sacrificed, since he holds: since he consecrated its mother with the sanctity of the value of a guilt offering, which is his obligation, and a guilt offering is not sacrificed from a female, it was consecrated only for its value; and since it is consecrated with the sanctity of value, it is consecrated with inherent sanctity, and this descends to the offspring, which is fit, being a male, so let it be sacrificed. That is why it was necessary: “And Rabbi Elazar concedes.”

notes.he: [מגו דקדושת דמים קדיש קדיש קדושת הגוף וליקרב]:
notes.en: And let us say so too: [since it is consecrated with the sanctity of value, it is consecrated with inherent sanctity, and let it be sacrificed].

messages.text: If so, that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina’s ruling is necessary to exclude the possibility that Rabbi Elazar’s reason is that the offspring is suitable as an offering, then say the following: Rather than teach us that the offspring of a female designated as a guilt offering is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, let him teach us a more expansive ruling, that its offspring is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, despite the fact that the mother is left to graze until it becomes unfit, at which point it is sold, and the proceeds are used for the purchase of a burnt offering. And from that ruling one would know that the same is true that the offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering.

notes.he: דטעמיה משום שם אמו הוא לישמעינן רבי יוסי בר"ח דאין בנה קרב עולה דליכא שם עולה על אמו דאשם קרייה והוא הדין דידענא דלאשם לא קרב דהשתא ומה לעולה דאימיה לדמי עולה אזלא אמרי' דלא קרב לעולה לאשם דאימיה דלא היא ולא דמיה אזלי לאשם כ"ש דלא קרב:
notes.en: If so: if his reason is because of the status of its mother, let Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina teach us that its offspring is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, since there is no burnt offering status for its mother, as he called it a guilt offering; and the same would apply, and I would know, that it is not sacrificed as a guilt offering. For if as a burnt offering, where its mother goes for the value of a burnt offering, we say it is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, then as a guilt offering, where neither its mother nor its value goes for a guilt offering, all the more so it is not sacrificed.

notes.dh: אדמשמע לן דאין בנה קרב אשם לישמעינן דאין בנה קרב עולה וכ"ש אשם
notes.he: לפרש"י ה"פ ומה עולה לא הוי אע"ג דאיכא שם עולה על אמו בעולת העוף כל שכן דאשם לא הוי דליכא שם אשם על אמו ולפי' הרמ"ר ומה עולה לא הוי אפילו נתכפר אף על גב דסוף האם להיות עולה כ"ש דאשם לא הוי קודם כפרה דאין סוף האם להיות אשם אם בנה קרב אשם:
notes.en: Rather than teach us that its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, let him teach us that its offspring is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, and all the more so a guilt offering: According to Rashi, the meaning is: if it is not a burnt offering, although there is burnt offering status for its mother in the bird burnt offering, all the more so it is not a guilt offering, where there is no guilt offering status for its mother. And according to the explanation of the RaMaR: if it is not a burnt offering even after atonement, although in the end the mother is to be a burnt offering, all the more so it is not a guilt offering before atonement, since in the end the mother would not be a guilt offering if its offspring were sacrificed as a guilt offering.

notes.he: דמשום הכי קאמר ומודה אמאי אשמעינן [דאין בנה דאשם קרב אשם:
notes.en: If so: if that is why he said “and concedes,” why did he teach us [that the offspring of a guilt offering is not sacrificed as a guilt offering?

notes.he: אם כן דאית ליה האי סברא נפלוג ר' אלעזר במפריש נקבה לאשם דבנה קרב אשם משום מגו וכ"ש במפריש נקבה לעולה דבנה קרב עולה דהא איכא שם עולה על אמו אי נמי משום דלמקום כו'. אלא מדפליג במפריש נקבה לעולה ולא פליג במפריש נקבה לאשם ש"מ דמודי דאין בנה קרב אשם:
notes.en: If so, if he holds this reasoning, let Rabbi Elazar disagree about one who designates a female for a guilt offering and say that its offspring is sacrificed as a guilt offering, because of “since”; and all the more so about one who designates a female for a burnt offering, that its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering, since there is burnt offering status for its mother, or else because “to the place,” etc. Rather, since he disagrees about one who designates a female for a burnt offering and does not disagree about one who designates a female for a guilt offering, conclude that he concedes that its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering.

messages.text: If he would teach us that according to Rabbi Elazar the offspring is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, I would say that it is only as a burnt offering that the offspring is not sacrificed, because he did not consecrate the mother with the same type of sanctity for the sake of which the fetus would be sacrificed. This is because the mother was consecrated as a guilt offering whereas the offspring would have been sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.he: אע"ג דאיכא שם עולה על אמו נקבה והוא הדין כ"ש דאין בנה קרב אשם דליכא שם אשם על אמו. ואכתי אמאי אמר אין בנה קרב אשם] איצטריך דאי אשמעינן (אין עולה) [דאין בנה] קרב עולה באשם הוה אמינא עולה הוא דלא קרב דלא אקדשיה לאימיה קדושת עולה אלא קדושת אשם אבל אשם ליקרב דהא אקדשיה לאימיה לאשם קמ"ל דמודי רבי אלעזר דאין קרב אשם:
notes.en: Let him teach us that its offspring is not sacrificed as a burnt offering: although there is burnt offering status for its female mother; and the same applies, all the more so, that its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, where there is no guilt offering status for its mother. So why did he still say that its offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering?] It was necessary, for had he taught us [that its offspring] is not sacrificed as a burnt offering in the case of a guilt offering, I would say: it is only as a burnt offering that it is not sacrificed, since he did not consecrate its mother with the sanctity of a burnt offering but with the sanctity of a guilt offering; but as a guilt offering let it be sacrificed, since he consecrated its mother for a guilt offering. He teaches us that Rabbi Elazar concedes that it is not sacrificed as a guilt offering.

messages.text: But with regard to the option of sacrificing the offspring as a guilt offering, when the offspring has the same type of sanctity as that with which the mother was consecrated, I might say that the offspring is sacrificed as a guilt offering. Therefore, he teaches us that it is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, even according to the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.

messages.caption: A female set aside for a Paschal offering gives birth to a male: the Rabbis and Rabbi Elazar in the baraitot of 19a with the Gemara’s readings, and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina on a female set aside for a guilt offering.

messages.text: Mishna

In the case of one who designates a female animal for a guilt offering, which may be brought only from males, it is left to graze until it becomes blemished and then it is sold, and he brings a guilt offering with the money received for its sale.

notes.he: שנתכפר באחר נעשה מותר יפלו דמיו של אשם נקבה לנדבת צבור לשופר לעולה:
notes.en: Mishna: And if his guilt offering was sacrificed: that is, he achieved atonement with another, so this one became a leftover; the money of the female guilt offering is allocated for communal gift offerings, for the horn-shaped collection box, for a burnt offering.

messages.text: And if in the interim, he designated a male animal and his guilt offering was already sacrificed, so that a guilt offering is no longer needed, the money received for the sale of the blemished female is allocated for communal gift offerings.

Since a female is unfit to be sacrificed as a guilt offering, its halakhic status is like that of a blemished animal in the sense that it does not become inherently sacred; rather, its value alone becomes sacred. Therefore, it may be sold without a blemish, and a guilt offering is purchased with the money received for its sale.

notes.he: דהואיל ולא חזיא למילתיה מום גמור הוא זה ולא קדשה קדושת הגוף ותמכר מיד ותביא בדמיה אשם. ואע"ג דגבי מפריש נקבה לעולה לא פליג ר' שמעון דודאי בעיא מום התם הוא דאיכא שם עולה עלה בעוף אבל אשם נקבה לא מצינו והיינו מומא ולא קדשה אלא לדמי:
notes.en: Mishna: It may be sold without a blemish: since it is not fit for its purpose, this is a full blemish, and it was not consecrated with inherent sanctity; so it is sold at once and he brings a guilt offering with its money. And although Rabbi Shimon does not disagree about one who designates a female for a burnt offering, where it certainly requires a blemish, that is because there is burnt offering status for it, in birds. But a female guilt offering we do not find; this is the blemish, and it was consecrated only for its value.

notes.dh: רבי שמעון אומר תימכר שלא במום
notes.he: והא דלא פליג נמי רבי שמעון במפריש נקבה לעולה ולימא תימכר שלא במום למאן דאית ליה בגמרא אליבא דר"ש דמפריש נקבה לעולה דוקא עושה תמורה אבל מפריש נקבה לאשם אינו עושה תמורה שפיר דלא פליג אעולה כמו אאשם דעולה יש לה קדושת הגוף טפי מאשם דעולה עושה תמורה ואין אשם עושה תמורה אבל לר"ש בן יהודה דאית ליה אליבא דר' אליעזר [אף לעולתו אין עושה תמורה וא"כ] במפריש נקבה לעולה נמי תימכר שלא במום צ"ל דפליג באשם וה"ה בעולה ותנא גבי אשם לאשמועינן דאפילו הכי יפלו דמיו לנדבה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: it may be sold without a blemish: As for why Rabbi Shimon does not also disagree about one who designates a female for a burnt offering and say it is sold without a blemish: according to the one who holds in the Gemara, according to Rabbi Shimon, that one who designates a female for a burnt offering does render a substitute but one who designates a female for a guilt offering does not, it is well that he does not disagree about a burnt offering as he does about a guilt offering, since a burnt offering has more inherent sanctity than a guilt offering, as a burnt offering renders a substitute and a guilt offering does not. But according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, who holds according to Rabbi Eliezer [so the printed Tosafot] [that even for his burnt offering it does not render a substitute, and if so,] with one who designates a female for a burnt offering too it should be sold without a blemish, one must say that he disagrees about a guilt offering and the same is true of a burnt offering, and the tanna taught it about a guilt offering to teach us that even so its money goes for gift offerings.

notes.he: כיון דהפריש נקבה שאינה קריבה הרי היא כבעל מום ותימכר לאלתר בלא רעייה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: since he designated a female, which is not sacrificed, it is like a blemished animal and is sold at once, without grazing.

messages.text: Gemara

And why do I need to wait until the female animal that was designated as a guilt offering becomes blemished before it can be sold? Let it be sold immediately even without a blemish: Since it is a female and therefore unfit for the matter for which it was designated, this is the same thing as a blemish.
messages.quote: it is left to graze until it becomes blemished

messages.text: This is the reason that the female animal may not be sold before it becomes blemished, for we say that as sanctity that inheres in its value has descended on it, therefore inherent sanctity has descended on it as well. Although it may not be sacrificed in any event, its inherent sanctity still mandates that it may not be sold until it becomes blemished.

notes.dh: גמ' נחתא לה נמי קדושת הגוף
notes.he: להא מילתא דבעיא מום:
notes.en: Gemara: Inherent sanctity has descended on it as well: for this purpose, that it requires a blemish.

messages.text: That is to say that even if one consecrated a male animal with the intention of selling it and bringing a burnt offering or guilt offering with the money received for its sale, as it becomes sanctified with sanctity that inheres in its value, it also becomes sanctified with inherent sanctity. And as the animal is fit to be brought as a burnt offering or as a guilt offering, it is sacrificed.

notes.he: מדבעיא מום ואף על גב דלדמי מקדשה אלמא קדשה קדושת הגוף ומיהו האי דלא אקרבה משום דאין אשם בא נקבה זאת אומרת הקדיש זכר לדמי עולה או אשם מיגו דנחתא ליה קדושת דמים נחתא ליה קדושת הגוף וכיון דאיהו גופיה חזי להקרבה קרב:
notes.en: That is to say, etc.: since it requires a blemish even though he consecrated it for its value, evidently it was consecrated with inherent sanctity; the reason it is not sacrificed is only that a guilt offering does not come from a female. That is to say: if he consecrated a male for the value of a burnt offering or a guilt offering, since sanctity of value descends on it, inherent sanctity descends on it; and since it itself is fit for sacrifice, it is sacrificed.

notes.dh: זאת אומרת הקדיש זכר לדמיו קדוש קדושת הגוף
notes.he: ותימה למורי הר"ר שמואל מאי שנא ממקדיש לדמי נסכים דאמר בפ"ק דשבועות (דף יא.) דאינו קדוש קדושת הגוף ושמא י"ל דההיא דהתם אתיא כר"ש דאמר לקמן בסמוך דכל מידי דלא חזי לגופיה לא נחתא ביה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: That is to say: if he consecrated a male for its value, it is sanctified with inherent sanctity: My teacher Rabbi Shmuel found this puzzling: how is it different from one who consecrates [an animal] for the value of libations, of which it says in the first chapter of Shevuot (11a) that it is not sanctified with inherent sanctity? Perhaps one can say that the case there follows Rabbi Shimon, who says shortly below that inherent sanctity does not descend on anything that is not fit in itself.

notes.he: כיון דנקבה צריכה רעייה משום דאמרינן מגו כ"ש מפריש זכר לדמיו דכיון דחזי גופיה להקרבה מגו דקדיש קדושת דמים קדיש קדושת הגוף]:
notes.en: [That is to say: since a female requires grazing because we say “since,” all the more so with one who designates a male for its value: since it itself is fit for sacrifice, as it is consecrated with the sanctity of value, it is consecrated with inherent sanctity.]

messages.text: It was stated that this issue is subject to a dispute of amora’im: If one consecrated a male animal with the intention of selling it and bringing a burnt offering or guilt offering with the money received for its sale:
It is sanctified with inherent sanctity.
It is not sanctified with inherent sanctity.

But Rava later retracted his statement and agreed with the opinion of Rav Kahana, due to the aforementioned statement of Rav Yehuda citing that which Rav said, that as the animal becomes sanctified with sanctity that inheres in its value, inherent sanctity also takes effect.

notes.he: דתרצה למתניתין דאמרינן מגו:
notes.en: Due to Rav Yehuda citing Rav: who explained the mishna, in that we say “since.”

notes.he: ואמר רבא זאת אומרת. ש"מ הדר ביה רבא:
notes.en: Due to Rav Yehuda citing Rav; and Rava said, “That is to say.” Conclude that Rava retracted.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Shimon disagrees with the opinion of the Rabbis and says that a female animal that was designated as a guilt offering may be sold without a blemish, as it is unfit to be sacrificed as the offering for which it was designated, and this itself is considered a blemish.
messages.quote: it may be sold without a blemish

messages.text: @Rabbi Yoḥanan Why doesn’t Rabbi Shimon say that as sanctity that inheres in its value has descended on it, inherent sanctity should descend on it as well, and therefore it may not be sold until it becomes blemished?

Rabbi Shimon conforms to his standard line of reasoning, as he says with regard to anything that is not fit itself to be sacrificed upon the altar, that inherent sanctity does not descend upon it. As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.lead: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin:
messages.quote: inherent sanctity should descend on it as well

notes.he: להקרבה לא נחתה לה קדושת הגוף. ותימכר שלא במום:
notes.en: That is not fit itself: for sacrifice, inherent sanctity does not descend on it, and it is sold without a blemish.

notes.he: ל"א כל דלא חזי להקרבה לאלתר לא קדיש קדושת הגוף והאי דאמר הכא לאלתר לאו דוקא קאמר דהא לא לאלתר [ולא] לאחר זמן לא חזי אלא אגב דקא בעי למימר אשם בן שתי שנים והביאו בן שנה ומחוסר זמן דלאלתר לא חזי ולאחר זמן חזי קאמר הכא לאלתר:
notes.en: Another version: anything that is not fit for sacrifice immediately is not consecrated with inherent sanctity. And what it says here, “immediately,” is not precise, since this one is fit neither immediately nor later; but because it is about to speak of a guilt offering in its second year that he brought in its first, and of an animal whose time has not yet arrived, which is not fit immediately but is fit later, it says “immediately” here.

messages.text: In the case of a guilt offering that should be sacrificed when it is in its first year, such as a guilt offering of a nazirite or of a leper, but the owner brought it when it was in its second year, or a guilt offering that should be sacrificed when it is in its second year, such as a guilt offering for robbery, for misuse of consecrated property, or for a designated maidservant, and the owner brought it when it was in its first year, the offering is fit, but it does not satisfy the obligation of the owner to bring a guilt offering, and he must bring another one.

notes.he: אשם גזילות ומעילות ושפחה חרופה דכתיב בהו איל (ויקרא ה יט):
notes.en: A guilt offering in its second year: the guilt offering for robbery, for misuse of consecrated property and for a designated maidservant, about which “a ram” is written (Leviticus 5:19).

notes.he: אשם נזיר ומצורע דכתיב בהו כבש (במדבר ו ויקרא יד):
notes.en: A guilt offering in its first year: the guilt offering of a nazirite and of a leper, about which “a lamb” is written (Numbers 6; Leviticus 14).

notes.dh: אשם בן שנה והביאו בן שתים בן שתים והביאו בן שנה כשר ולא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה
notes.he: תימה בפרק התכלת (מנחות דף מח:) תני פסול ותעובר צורתו ויצא לבית השריפה וי"מ דההיא דהתם אתיא כר' שמעון דאמר הכא דכל עצמן אינן קדושים ומיירי התם שהביאו ושחטו בעזרה והוי כשוחטים קדשי בדק הבית בפנים דפסול והא דבעי עיבור צורה היינו טעמא דלא ליחלפו בשאר קדשים פסולין דבעי עיבור צורה והרב ר' אפרים תירץ דהכא בשלא לשמו ומשום הכי כשר והתם מיירי בלשמו ודומיא מצינו בפרק בתרא דזבחים (דף קיד:) דאמר מחוסר זמן בבעלים פטור פירוש אם שחטו בחוץ ואמר רב חלקיה בר טוביה עלה לא שנו אלא לשמו אבל שלא לשמו חייב משום שחוטי חוץ הואיל וחזי בפנים אלמא היכא דשחט אשם שלא לשמו ראוי לפנים הוא מיהו ק"ק כיון דהכא מיירי בשלא לשמו מאי איריא דלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה משום דשינה בן שנה מבן שתי שנים תיפוק ליה דלא עלו משום דשלא לשמו הוא עי"ל דהכא מיירי לאחר שניתק לרעייה והתם מיירי בלא ניתק והוי אשם פסול:
notes.en: A guilt offering in its first year that he brought in its second, in its second year that he brought in its first, is fit, but they do not satisfy the obligation of the owner: It is puzzling, for in chapter HaTekhelet (Menaḥot 48b) it teaches that it is disqualified, its form must be left to decay, and it goes out to the place of burning. Some explain that the case there follows Rabbi Shimon, who says here that they are not consecrated at all, and it speaks there of one who brought it and slaughtered it in the courtyard, which is like slaughtering items consecrated for Temple maintenance inside, which is disqualified; and the requirement that its form decay is so that it not be confused with other disqualified consecrated animals that require their form to decay. Rabbi Efrayim answered that here it is where it was slaughtered not for its own sake, and that is why it is fit, while there it speaks of slaughter for its own sake. We find something similar in the last chapter of Zevaḥim (114b), which says that an animal whose time has not yet arrived with regard to its owner — he is exempt, that is, if he slaughtered it outside; and Rav Ḥilkiya bar Toviya said about it: they taught this only for its own sake, but not for its own sake he is liable for slaughtering outside, since it is fit inside. Evidently, where he slaughtered a guilt offering not for its own sake, it is fit inside. Yet it is somewhat difficult: since here it speaks of slaughter not for its own sake, why say that they do not satisfy the owner’s obligation because he switched a first-year animal for a second-year one? That they do not satisfy it follows already from its being not for its own sake. Or one can also say: here it speaks of after it was set aside to graze, and there it speaks of before it was set aside, and it is a disqualified guilt offering.

notes.he: כגון אשם נזיר ואשם מצורע דבן שנה הוא דכתיב בהו כבש:
notes.en: [A guilt offering in its first year: such as the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper, which is in its first year, as “a lamb” is written about them.

notes.he: דכבר קרוי איל או אשם בן שתי שנים כגון אשם גזלות ומעילה דכתיב בהו איל:
notes.en: And he brought it in its second year: when it is already called a ram. Or a guilt offering in its second year, such as the guilt offering for robbery and for misuse of consecrated property, about which “a ram” is written.

messages.text: The offering is disqualified, as these offerings themselves are not consecrated, due to the fact that the proper time of their offering has either not yet arrived or has already passed.

notes.he: כל עיקר אינן קדושין:
notes.en: They themselves are not consecrated [kol atzman]: they are not consecrated at all.

notes.he: היינו כל עיקר אינו קדוש דסבר כיון דלא חזי לגופיה לאשם להקרבה לא נחתא ליה קדושה]:
notes.en: They themselves: that is, it is not consecrated at all, since he holds that since it is not fit in itself to be sacrificed as a guilt offering, sanctity does not descend on it.]

messages.text: This indicates that Rabbi Shimon maintains that in such a case there is no inherent sanctity.

But consider the case of one who consecrates an animal whose time has not yet arrived, e.g., an animal that is less than eight days old, which is unfit to be sacrificed, and yet Rabbi Shimon said that it is sanctified with regard to the prohibition against the slaughter of sacrificial animals outside the Temple courtyard. This proves that according to Rabbi Shimon, even an offering that is not fit to be sacrificed has inherent sanctity.

notes.he: כדאמרינן בשחיטת חולין בפרק אותו ואת בנו (חולין דף פא.) דקתני שהיה רבי שמעון אומר כל הראוי לבא לאחר זמן השוחטו בחוץ עובר בלא תעשה:
notes.en: An animal whose time has not yet arrived, and Rabbi Shimon said that it is sanctified: as we say in Shechitat Ḥullin, in chapter Oto VeEt Beno (Ḥullin 81a), where it is taught that Rabbi Shimon would say: anything fit to come [to the altar] after a time, one who slaughters it outside [the Temple] transgresses a prohibition.

notes.dh: והא מחוסר זמן דלא חזי ואמר ר"ש קדיש לגופיה
notes.he: במסכת חולין פרק אותו ואת בנו (חולין דף פא.) דקתני ר"ש אומר כל הראוי לבא לאחר זמן השוחטו בחוץ עובר בלא תעשה:
notes.en: But an animal whose time has not yet arrived, which is unfit, and Rabbi Shimon said it is inherently consecrated: in tractate Ḥullin, chapter Oto VeEt Beno (Ḥullin 81a), it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says: anything fit to come after a time, one who slaughters it outside transgresses a prohibition.

notes.he: דפחות מבן שמונת ימים ואמר ר' שמעון דקדיש קדושת הגוף במס' זבחים בפרק אחרון. דתנן השוחט אותו ואת בנו ומחוסר זמן קדשים בחוץ ר' שמעון אומר שני בלא תעשה דשחוטי חוץ שהיה ר' שמעון אומר כל הראוי לבוא לאחר זמן הרי הוא בלא תעשה ומדקאי בלא תעשה אלמא דקדיש קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: But an animal whose time has not yet arrived: less than eight days old, and Rabbi Shimon said that it is consecrated with inherent sanctity, in tractate Zevaḥim, in the last chapter, as we learned: one who slaughters an animal and its offspring [on the same day], or a consecrated animal whose time has not yet arrived, outside — Rabbi Shimon says: [it is] under the prohibition of slaughtering outside [the text adds a word, “sheni,” whose sense here is unclear], for Rabbi Shimon would say: anything fit to come after a time is under a prohibition. And since it stands under a prohibition, evidently it is consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: An animal whose time has not yet arrived is different, as it is fit to be offered tomorrow, i.e., automatically at a later stage, and is therefore considered to be fit for an offering.

notes.he: מ"ה קדיש קדושת הגוף דלמחר חזי]:
notes.en: [An animal whose time has not yet arrived is different: that is why it is consecrated with inherent sanctity, since it is fit tomorrow.]

messages.text: If so, that any animal which will be fit to be sacrificed when its time arrives is sanctified with inherent sanctity, the same should also apply to a guilt offering that should be offered when it is in its second year but the owner brought it to be sacrificed when it was in its first year, as it will be fit for sacrifice in another year. Why, then, doesn’t it have inherent sanctity according to Rabbi Shimon?

notes.dh: אי הכי אשם בן שתים והביא בן שנה
notes.he: אמאי אמר כל עצמו אינו קדוש הא מיחזי (לשנא) [לקדשו] אלא ודאי לאו היינו טעמא במחוסר זמן משום דקדיש למחר דא"כ קשיא ליה אשם:
notes.en: If so, a guilt offering in its second year that he brought in its first: why did he say that it itself is not consecrated? It is fit [to be consecrated]. Rather, certainly this is not the reason for an animal whose time has not yet arrived, that it is consecrated because of tomorrow, for if so the guilt offering would be difficult for him.

messages.text: Rather, this is the reason of Rabbi Shimon in the case of an animal whose time has not yet arrived, as he derives it from the halakha of a firstborn.

notes.he: דיליף ליה מבכור:
notes.en: Rather, this is the reason for an animal whose time has not yet arrived: that he derives it from a firstborn.

messages.text: An animal whose time has not yet arrived enters the pen to be tithed together with the other animals. And it is considered in this regard to be like a firstborn: Just as a firstborn is sanctified before the time when it is fit to be sacrificed has arrived, i.e., immediately after birth, and it is sacrificed after its time, following the eighth day, so too, an animal whose time has not yet arrived is sanctified before its time has arrived and is sacrificed after its time.
messages.lead: As it is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:

notes.he: ברחם דהיינו לפני זמנו:
notes.en: A firstborn is sanctified: in the womb, which is before its time.

notes.dh: אף מחוסר זמן קדוש לפני זמנו וקרב לאחר זמנו
notes.he: תימה דאיתא בפ"ג דבכורות (דף כא) ונילף מקדשים דלא קדישי משמע דקדשים אינם קדושים במחוסר זמן ועוד דאמר בעלמא (זבחים דף יב.) לילה לקדושה יום להרצאה משמע דליל שמיני דוקא קדיש אבל מקמי הכי לא ויש לומר דה"מ לכתחילה אסור להקדישו מחוסר זמן מיהו אם עבר והקדיש קדיש דילפינן ליה מבכור: [וע"ע תוס' בכורות כא: ד"ה אף וכו']:
notes.en: So too, an animal whose time has not yet arrived is sanctified before its time and is sacrificed after its time: It is puzzling, for in the third chapter of Bekhorot (21a) it says, “And let us derive it from consecrated animals, which are not consecrated,” implying that consecrated animals are not consecrated while their time has not yet arrived. Moreover, it says elsewhere (Zevaḥim 12a): “The night for sanctity, the day for acceptance,” implying that it is consecrated only from the night of the eighth day, but not before. One can say: that applies only from the outset, that it is forbidden to consecrate it while its time has not yet arrived; but if he transgressed and consecrated it, it is consecrated, since we derive it from a firstborn. [See also Tosafot, Bekhorot 21b, s.v. Af.]

notes.he: מה בכור קדוש לפני זמנו דקדושתו מרחם וקרב בזמנו לאחר ח' ימים אף זה מחוסר זמן (כיון) נכנס לדיר להתעשר דיליף מעשר עברה עברה מבכור אבל באשם דלא כתיב ביה עברה כל עצמו אינו קדוש:
notes.en: Just as a firstborn is consecrated before its time, as its sanctity is from the womb, and is sacrificed in its time, after eight days, so too this animal whose time has not yet arrived enters the pen to be tithed, since he derives the tithe from the firstborn by the verbal analogy of “passing” and “passing” [avara–avara]. But with a guilt offering, where “passing” is not written, it itself is not consecrated at all.

messages.text: One who consecrates a female animal for his burnt offering …
messages.lead: § The Gemara continues to discuss this dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis: The Sages taught:

notes.he: עושה תמורה דאיכא שם עולה עליה בעוף:
notes.en: For his burnt offering: it renders a substitute, since there is burnt offering status for it, in birds.

notes.he: (ע"כ שייך לדף הקודם) ר' שמעון אמר לעולתו (דהוי) [דאינה] חובתו עושה תמורה שהרי בנה קרב עולה ואיכא שם עולה (על) [עליה בעוף עושה] תמורה:
notes.en: (A printed marker here reads: “up to here belongs to the previous daf.”) Rabbi Shimon says: for his burnt offering, [which is not] his obligation, it renders a substitute, since its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering, and there is burnt offering status [for it in birds; it renders] a substitute.

messages.text: The baraita continues on 20a: “…or for his Paschal offering or for his guilt offering,” it renders a substitute; Rabbi Shimon distinguishes the burnt offering from the other two.
